newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Block trading, rate worries hit Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Block trading, rate worries hit Brussels bourse.

text.p: An avalanche of late block trading and a sudden tumble in bond prices ahead of the three-day Whit weekend combined to batter the Brussels bourse lower at the close on a busy Friday.
But traders said fundamentally the picture remained solidly optimistic, and there was no cause to fear a sudden collapse.
"The Dow Jones is moving a bit lower, bond yields look to be moving up and we are pausing for breath before the long weekend," one trader said.
"But there is no real reason to be worried about a sell off," he added.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended 11.00 points or 0.49 percent down at 2,240.30 with 11 losers, five unchanged and four gainers.
The index had spent most of the day comfortably in the black, but was hit in the late afternoon.
An impressive total of 8.5 billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands -- nearly triple the daily average for the rest of the week.
Traders said the volume was boosted by a large quantity of block trades that came into the market in the last half hour of business.

Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, which saw some 81,000 shares traded, ended the day unchanged at 21,100 francs on what traders said was a continued recovery after being hit recently by a broker downgrade.
Bank BBL, which also saw 188,000 shares traded -- mainly in blocks -- was likewise unchanged at 8,930 francs.
Main loser of the day was electronics firm Barco, down 2.6 percent to 6,370 francs on profittaking.
By contrast fast food chain Quick, which was hit on Monday and Tuesday by reports of a flat first quarter, recovered 4.7 percent to 1,995 francs.
